To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Amdahl's fixed-workload condition is not a realistic assumption for multicore architectures, (2) the fixed-time condition is a better assumption for multicore scalability, (3) multicore scalability is not limited by memory wall, and (4) multicore scalability can be improved by reducing memory access overheads.

multicore architectures can achieve 1) a fixed-time speedup of 2.7x (for the same chip area and clock frequency), 2) a fixed-workload speedup of 3.3x (for the fixed chip area), and 3) a memory-bound speedup of 1.5x (for the chip with fixed number of cores).
the fixed-workload condition is not the best model for multicore scalability, and that multicore scalability is not limited by Amdahl's Law.
